key_insight: GraphBEAT turns irregular longitudinal EHR events into time-bucketed directed graphs to improve early cancer risk stratification from sparse, heterogeneous data.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help identify patients at elevated risk of pancreatic, liver, or intestinal cancer earlier using routinely collected diagnosis codes and lab results.
method: Groups clinical events into temporal buckets and builds patient-specific directed graphs.
Encodes each node with feature identity, observed value, and time position.
Uses time-decay message passing plus multi-head attention pooling to create patient-level predictions.
evidence_signal: Trained and tested on multi-site longitudinal EHR data for 12-, 24-, and 36-month lead-time prediction, GraphBEAT outperformed GraphSAGE, GAT, GCN, Transformer, and LSTM baselines while using far fewer FLOPs and parameters.
watch_item: Performance was shown in retrospective EHR evaluation, so external validation and real-world workflow testing are still needed before clinical use.
paper_title: GraphBEAT: Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers
